Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract and rollout evidence. I’ll also apply the fish-control bookshelf protocol you named, plus the wake-visual inspection skill so both 3D views inform any policy change before I edit it.

The inherited evidence already records several completed near-miss variants with no semantic improvement, so this is a required re-consultation point for the bookshelf. The shelf favors a mechanism change: a response-deficit-triggered anterior half-cycle correction, not another scalar redirect-depth or carrier-gain tweak. I’m now checking that hypothesis against the sampled trajectories and both visual rows.

The visual/trace comparison rejects two tempting repeats. The assigned posterior-asymmetry parent stays in the high corridor, reaches the joint boundary, and carries roughly 10× the near-miss loads; the low-load terminal-wave sample keeps a coherent self-propelled wake but still passes the target. The latest inherited intercept-hold test also regressed from the `0.827823L` reference to `1.096087L`, so I’m treating instantaneous projected intercept as beat-contaminated rather than retuning its thresholds.

I’ve recorded the pre-edit diagnosis and bookshelf transfer block. The candidate will restore the low-load response-released controller and add one mechanism: an inertial line-of-sight-rate response residual on joint 1. It will never cancel an already adequate turn; it activates only when target-line rotation requests more yaw than the phase-rejected measured response supplies.

The policy and reusable evidence lesson are both updated. I’m invoking the required check-runner now; it will perform only the guidance semantic check, lightweight Julia contract check, and editable-boundary audit—no CFD.

The configured check-runner could not start because its pinned model is unavailable in this account. I’ve still invoked the configuration and will run its three prescribed commands directly, separately, so the required validation is completed without CFD.

All three prescribed checks pass. I’m doing one extra algebraic audit now for the new mechanism’s reflection symmetry, finite zero-speed behavior, parameter-schema coverage, and actual activation on a representative closing/rotating line-of-sight state.

The extra audit passes: the residual activates only on joint 1 in the representative response-deficit state, preserves exact reflection symmetry, stays finite at zero speed, and every parameter reference is schema-owned. I’m doing the final post-evidence bookshelf cross-check and rerunning the guidance check after the audit note update.

Implemented exactly one Phase 2 candidate: an inertial line-of-sight response closure using bounded anterior half-cycle actuation.

Updated:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl)
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md)
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md)

All prescribed non-CFD checks passed: guidance semantics, Julia policy contract, parameter-schema coverage, editable boundary, boundedness, activation, and reflection equivariance. The pinned check-runner model was unavailable, so its exact commands were run directly. No CFD was run.
